qs.q: A 60-year-old chronic smoker presents with a central lung mass and hypercalcaemia. Laboratory evaluation indicates the hypercalcaemia is mediated by ectopic parathyroid hormone-related peptide. What is the most likely histologic type of this carcinoma?
qs.e: Squamous cell carcinoma of the lung is typically central, strongly smoking-associated, and frequently causes hypercalcaemia via parathyroid hormone-related peptide secretion. Adenocarcinoma is more commonly peripheral and associated with non-smokers.
qs.s: Cardiovascular, Respiratory & GI/Hepatobiliary Pathology Revision: MCQs

qs.q: A patient presents with bone pain, fatigue, and hypercalcaemia. Skeletal imaging reveals multiple punched-out lytic bone lesions. Which laboratory finding supports the diagnosis of multiple myeloma?
o: Normal 24-hour urinary excretion of Bence Jones proteins
Plasma cell percentage below 5 percent on bone marrow aspirate
Decreased serum free light chains without paraprotein
Monoclonal spike on serum protein electrophoresis
qs.e: A monoclonal spike or paraprotein on serum protein electrophoresis is a key investigation finding in multiple myeloma. Bone marrow plasma cells must be greater than 10 percent rather than below 5 percent for a diagnosis.
qs.s: Acute Leukaemia (AML/ALL) & WBC Disorders: Haematology Guide: MCQs

qs.q: A heavy smoker presents with a central lung mass. Biopsy reveals malignant cells producing keratin and causing hypercalcaemia due to parathyroid hormone-related peptide secretion. Which carcinoma is this?
qs.e: Squamous cell carcinoma of the lung is typically central, associated with smoking, and characterized by keratin pearls and PTHrP-induced hypercalcaemia. Adenocarcinoma is typically peripheral and the most common overall lung cancer in non-smokers.
qs.s: Cardiovascular & Respiratory Pathology: Atherosclerosis, RHD & MI: MCQs

qs.q: A 30-year-old female is investigated for hypercalcaemia. In primary hypoparathyroidism, which paired laboratory derangement of calcium and phosphate is characteristically found?
qs.e: Hypoparathyroidism results in hypocalcaemia due to a lack of parathyroid hormone-mediated bone resorption and renal calcium reabsorption, coupled with hyperphosphataemia from decreased renal phosphate excretion. Hyperparathyroidism would show the opposite pattern of high calcium and low phosphate.
qs.s: Medical Pathology Final Revision: Chemical, Hema, Systemic: MCQs

qs.q: A patient with a lung tumour presents with hypercalcaemia. Which histological subtype is most strongly associated with this paraneoplastic syndrome?
qs.e: Hypercalcaemia is most often associated with squamous cell carcinoma due to the secretion of PTH-related peptide. SCLC is more commonly linked to Cushing syndrome or SIADH, while adenocarcinoma is linked to coagulation abnormalities.

qs.q: Hypercalcaemia in squamous-cell lung carcinoma WITHOUT bone metastases is caused by
qs.e: PTHrP mediates humoral hypercalcaemia of malignancy (HHM) by binding PTH receptors. True ectopic PTH is exceedingly rare. PTHrP suppresses endogenous PTH, distinguishing HHM from primary hyperparathyroidism.
